Add general coding guidelines

Language-agnostic guidelines covering naming (descriptive names,
no misleading names, encode units, boolean names), comments
(explain why, design decisions, cite sources, no commented-out code),
layout (one concept per file, top-down reading), formatting
(error messages), and API design (hide implementation details,
type invariants, fix root causes, validate at boundaries).

Add Rust guidelines structure and naming conventions

Add Rust language items guidelines

Add guidelines for variables (checked arithmetic, prefer immutable,
explain variables), functions (minimize nesting, small functions,
no flag args), types and traits (enum over dyn, type invariants,
simplify state, no redundant Option), comments and documentation
(doc comments, RFC 1574, backticks, no-impl-in-docs, module docs,
delete dead code), unsafety (safety comments, safety docs,
deny-unsafe-kernel, minimize unsafe, module boundary safety),
modules and crates (narrow visibility, getter encapsulation,
workspace deps, import groups), and macros and attributes
(narrow lint suppression, expect dead code, prefer functions
over macros).

Add Rust select topics guidelines

handling (propagate errors with ?), defensive programming

hot paths, minimize copies, no premature optimization), logging
(log crate only, log levels), and memory and resource management
(RAII).

Add `@boterinas codex` comment command to trigger Codex review

Replace the `synchronize` trigger with an on-demand `@boterinas codex`
comment command so that Codex reviews are only run when explicitly
requested by repository members, avoiding wasted API credits on every
push. The workflow now reacts with an eyes emoji for immediate feedback
and restricts usage to MEMBER/OWNER/COLLABORATOR author associations.

Harden Codex review workflow for fork PRs

- Remove the `pull_request_target` auto-trigger entirely. Codex
  reviews are now triggered only via `@boterinas codex` comments
  (gated to MEMBER/OWNER/COLLABORATOR) or `workflow_dispatch`.
  This prevents untrusted fork code from running with secrets and
  stops API-credit abuse from arbitrary PR opens.

- Always restore `.github/codex-output-schema.json` from the base
  branch unconditionally. This fixes the "No such file or directory"
  failure for PRs predating the schema file, and prevents fork PRs
  from supplying a crafted schema.

Validate @boterinas codex command at start of line

The job-level contains() is a substring match, so comments like
"> @boterinas codex" (blockquote) or "don't run @boterinas codex"
(mid-sentence) would false-trigger. Add a validation step that
requires the command at the start of a line before proceeding.

Use POSIX-compatible grep -E instead of grep -P for portability.

Fetch Codex output schema from upstream default branch via API

The previous approach used `git checkout "$BASE_SHA"` to restore the
schema file, which fails when the PR's base SHA predates the addition
of the schema file. Instead, fetch it from the upstream default branch
via the GitHub Contents API. This always works regardless of git
history and ensures the schema matches the workflow version on main.

Add coding guideline: qualify function imports with parent module

Add `alphabetical-attrs` coding guideline for attribute ordering

Add a new guideline requiring non-derive outer attributes to be sorted
alphabetically by name, with `#[derive(...)]` placed last (followed
only by derive helper attributes like `#[serde(...)]`). Traits within
`#[derive(...)]` are also sorted alphabetically. Placing derive last
ensures derive macros see the item after all attribute macros (e.g.,
`#[padding_struct]`, `#[pod_union]`) have transformed it.

The guideline is backed by the discussion in PR #3080 and PR #2898.

Enforce `alphabetical-attrs` guideline across the codebase

Sort all non-derive outer attributes alphabetically by name,
place `#[derive(...)]` last (before any derive helper attributes
like `#[serde(...)]` and `#[clap(...)]`), and sort traits inside
`#[derive(...)]` alphabetically. This covers 329 files with 704
line changes (all pure reordering, no semantic changes).

Key patterns normalized:
- `#[cfg(...)]` comes first (c), then other attrs alphabetically
- `#[repr(...)]` stays before `#[derive(...)]` (derive is always last)
- `#[padding_struct]` and `#[pod_union]` precede `#[derive(...)]`
- Derive helper attrs like `#[serde(...)]` remain after `#[derive(...)]`
- Derive traits like `Debug, Clone, Copy` become `Clone, Copy, Debug`
- The common set `{Debug, Clone, Copy, Pod, Default}` (59 uses,
  12 prior orderings) is now uniformly `Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Pod`

Fix positional I/O semantics for `pread`/`pwrite`

The existing implementation treats `pread`/`pwrite` as having the same
semantics as `check_seekable`, but Linux does not. Namespace files
(nsfs) support `pread`/`pwrite` but not `lseek`, which our current
code cannot express.

Add a `check_positional_io` default method to the `FileIo` trait that
delegates to `check_seekable`. This is correct for most files and only
needs an override for nsfs, which returns `Ok(())`.

In `InodeHandle::read_at`/`write_at`, move the positional I/O check
before the rights check so that pipes correctly return `ESPIPE` instead
of `EBADF` when opened with the wrong access mode.

Remove the early `user_buf_len == 0` return in `pread64`/`pwrite64` so
that unsupported files get the proper `ESPIPE` even for zero-length
requests.

Signed-off-by: Zhenchen Wang <m202372036@hust.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Zhihang Shao <dio_ro@outlook.com>

Fix `preadv`/`pwritev` errno for empty buffer lists

When `io_vec_count` is zero or all iov entries have `iov_len == 0`,
the previous code returned `Ok(0)` without checking whether the file
supports positional I/O. This caused pipes and `O_PATH` fds to
incorrectly succeed instead of returning `ESPIPE` or `EBADF`.

Probe with a zero-length `read_at`/`write_at` call before the loop
so that unsupported files still get the correct errno, matching the
fix already applied to `pread64`/`pwrite64`.

Signed-off-by: Zhenchen Wang <m202372036@hust.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Zhihang Shao <dio_ro@outlook.com>

Add regression tests for positional I/O error handling

Cover the following scenarios:

- pipe_err: zero-length `pread64`/`pwrite64`/`preadv`/`pwritev` on
  pipes must return `ESPIPE`.
- access_err: `O_PATH` file descriptors must return `EBADF` for all
  positional I/O variants (zero-length and nonzero-length).
- proc_nsfs: zero-length `pread` on namespace files must return
  `EINVAL` (not `ESPIPE`); `O_PATH` nsfs fds return `EBADF`.
- full: positional writes to `/dev/full` must return `ENOSPC`.

Fix race in `exit_process` where parent can be dropped before `find_reaper_process`

A zombie process can be reaped and removed from its parent's children
map. If the parent then exits, it won't move the reaped child to a new
reaper, leaving the child's `Weak` parent reference dangling. Defer
`set_zombie` until after `move_children_to_reaper_process` so the
process stays in its parent's children map and any exiting ancestor
will update the parent reference before becoming zombie itself.

Suppress fsnotify events for `O_PATH` fds

In Linux, `O_PATH` file descriptors carry `FMODE_NONOTIFY` in
`f_mode`, which suppresses all fsnotify events. Asterinas did not
implement this — `O_PATH` fds would trigger `on_open` and `on_close`
notifications like regular fds.

`O_PATH` is already observable on the `FileLike` trait via
`status_flags()`, so suppress open/close notifications directly on
that flag instead of introducing a dedicated mode type. The shared
`O_PATH` check and subscriber lookup in `on_open`/`on_close` are
factored into a `notifiable_path` helper. The `on_access`/`on_modify`
hooks need no check: an `O_PATH` `InodeHandle` is built with empty
`Rights`, so reads and writes fail with `EBADF` before any access or
modify notification could fire.

Add the aster-code-review skill

A local-first, agent-agnostic code-review skill for Asterinas, with a benchmark
that measures its recall. It reviews code against the persona-keyed Coding
Guidelines and writes one Markdown review file, making both objective (bug) and
subjective (guideline-grounded) calls.

Two review modes (scripts/resolve_target.sh), both anchored at HEAD:
- `diff <base>` — the commit series merge-base(base,HEAD)..HEAD: each commit's
  message and diff, so the review covers per-commit intent and commit hygiene.
- `files <path[:lines] ...>` — the working-tree contents of the named files.
The raw argument string is self-tokenized (double quotes, line ranges) so the
parse is deterministic regardless of how the skill is triggered.

Execution model (SKILL.md, spec/execution_model.md): a thin orchestrator
activates the five personas by path, fans out one isolated pass per persona
(scripts/build_pass_prompt.sh assembles a cache-ordered prompt — stable contract
and guideline first, the review input last), then deterministically assembles
(scripts/assemble_review.sh), verifies, consolidates, and summarizes into the
review file. `--per-persona-context=auto|yes|no` trades the fan-out (best recall)
for a cheaper combined pass.

Benchmark (benchmark/): one queryable problems.yaml, each problem pinned to a
source commit and checked by validate_problem_yaml.sh; run.sh reconstructs each
problem in an isolated worktree (fetching the commit if absent), reviews
cheap-first with escalation to the fan-out on a miss, and grades recall — without
leaking the answers to the reviewer (overlay_skill.sh overlays the current skill
but excludes the suite, the worktree path is opaque, and the defects go only to
the grader).

Design rationale lives in spec/ (motivation, coding_guidelines, interface,
execution_model, benchmark, related_work), with every significant decision argued
in place. The deterministic scripts and the problem schema are covered by
model-free tests in tests/.

Run aster-code-review from a /aster-code-review PR comment

A `/aster-code-review …` comment (gated to owners/members/collaborators) drives
the skill on the PR, mirroring the skill interface:

  diff / files   review the PR, post inline comments
  smoke          `make smoke`     — does the skill run?
  benchmark      `make benchmark` — recall (informational)

The workflow is split in two: a fast triage job parses the command with a
trusted, default-branch copy of the parser (scripts/parse_pr_command.sh), gates
on author association, and replies promptly; a run job re-validates every value,
runs the skill, and posts either inline review comments (findings off the PR diff
go in the review body) or a human-friendly status comment. Replaces the earlier
Codex-JSON-schema workflow (and drops codex-output-schema.json).

Add SparseIdAlloc, a range-bounded sparse u32 ID allocator

Serves an inclusive `[min, max]` range with a `BTreeMap` of maximal
allocated-ID runs. Allocates the smallest unallocated ID in range.

Overhaul mount ID allocation: drop upper bound, add unique IDs

Add a monotonically increasing `unique_id: u64` alongside the
recyclable `id: u32`, mirroring Linux's `mnt_id_unique` and `mnt_id`.
`statx` returns the unique ID when the caller sets
`STATX_MNT_ID_UNIQUE`.

Bundle the two IDs in a `MountId` value.

Add listmount syscall using namespace mount table

Implement `listmount(2)` for the current mount namespace. Given
`LSMT_ROOT` or a parent mount's `unique_id`, return the unique IDs of
its strict descendants ordered by `unique_id`, with support for
`LISTMOUNT_REVERSE` and the `param` pagination cursor.

Report IPv6 addresses and attributes in `RTM_GETADDR`

Fix `format_all.sh` silently skipping excluded crates on BSD sed

The workspace `exclude` list was extracted with a `sed` expression that relies
on a GNU extension. Under BSD sed it errors and prints nothing, and because a
pipeline reports its last command's status, `set -e` does not catch it. The
list ends up empty, so the loop over the excluded crates never runs and the
script still exits 0 — reporting success while checking none of them.

Read the list with Python's TOML parser instead, as
`tools/print_workspace_members.sh` already does. This adds no new dependency:
the Makefile already invokes that script.

Fix `VT_MANAGER` panic on early keyboard input

The VT keyboard handler is registered before `VT_MANAGER` is
initialized, and it can run from IRQ context as soon as registration
completes. A key event arriving in this window hits
`VT_MANAGER.get().expect(...)` in `handle_key_event` and panics the
kernel. `VtManager::new` does not depend on the keyboard state, so
initialize the manager first.

Add total kernel slab allocation counter

Track the total physical memory committed to the kernel slab caches by
adding a per-CPU counter that is incremented for each newly allocated
slab page and decremented when a slab page is released.

The counter only covers slab caches, matching the semantics of Linux's
`Slab` field in /proc/meminfo. Large allocations that bypass the slab
caches are not counted.

Using a per-CPU counter keeps allocation scalable; reading it sums up
all per-CPU values.

Implement Slab field in /proc/meminfo

Add the `Slab` field to /proc/meminfo, which reports the total physical
memory committed to the kernel slab caches in kilobytes.

Add a C regression test that reads /proc/meminfo and verifies the Slab
line exists with a non-zero value.

Add ktest for kernel slab allocation counter

dropping the cache returns the counter to its original value.

Move xattr permission checks to VFS paths

Apply access checks at the Path boundary so internal inode users, including exec-time file capability loading, can access xattrs without inheriting syscall permission policy.

Add file capability xattr handling

Validate Linux V2 and V3 capability xattrs, reject V1 writes, enforce CAP_SETFCAP, and convert root-owned V3 values on read. Keep valid writes unchanged because Asterinas currently has only the initial user namespace and no idmapped mounts. Preserve the validated header in a bounded kernel snapshot so concurrent userspace changes cannot replace it before the filesystem write.

Apply file capabilities during execve

Prepare and apply set-ID and file-capability credential transitions around execve, including nosuid, bounding, inheritable, effective, ambient, and no_new_privs behavior. Keep interpreter selection tied to the final executable image.

Clear file privileges after content mutations

Remove security.capability and set-ID bits after write, fallocate, and truncate paths. Treat absent or unsupported capability xattrs as already cleared, and preserve descriptor-based ftruncate authorization while sharing privilege invalidation.

Add file capability regression coverage

Cover xattr validation and conversion, exec credential transitions, nosuid and no_new_privs behavior, interpreter handling, and privilege invalidation. Use private executable copies only when a test mutates shared file state.

Fix signal character handling in the TTY line discipline

The line discipline generates signals only when both ICANON and ISIG
are set, but POSIX gates signal characters on ISIG alone. Interactive
shells keep ISIG on while readline switches the terminal to
non-canonical mode, so Ctrl+C at a shell prompt does nothing.

Recognize signal characters whenever ISIG is set, consume them instead
of delivering them to readers, discard pending input unless NOFLSH is
set, and generate SIGTSTP for VSUSP. This matches the Linux n_tty
behavior (drivers/tty/n_tty.c).

The new regression test passes unmodified on Linux and fails on
Asterinas without this fix.
